hints: Focus on what actually makes the glass dark, silver atoms ($\text{Ag}$), and track whether each reaction makes more or less of them.
Look at oxidation numbers in reaction 2, $\text{Cu}^{+}$ becomes $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ so it loses an electron, while $\text{Cl}$ becomes $\text{Cl}^{-}$ so it gains an electron.
Follow the copper ions through reactions 2 and 3 to see if they are used up overall or regenerated in a cycle.
walkthrough:
**Link darkness to silver atoms**

Remember the stem tells us darkness is due to $\text{Ag}$ atoms, not $\text{Ag}^{+}$ ions. So any reaction that makes $\text{Ag}$ darkens the glass, any reaction that removes $\text{Ag}$ lightens it.

Reaction 1: $$\text{Ag}^{+} + \text{Cl}^{-} \rightleftharpoons \text{Ag} + \text{Cl}$$

**Analyse reaction 2 for redox**

In reaction 2, check oxidation numbers. Copper goes from +1 to +2, so it loses an electron. Chlorine atom goes from 0 to -1, so it gains an electron.

$$\text{Cu}^{+} + \text{Cl} \rightarrow \text{Cu}^{2+} + \text{Cl}^{-}$$
This means $\text{Cu}^{+}$ is oxidised, so it is the reducing agent, and $\text{Cl}$ is reduced, so $\text{Cl}$ is the oxidising agent.

**Analyse reaction 3 for redox**

In reaction 3, silver goes from 0 in $\text{Ag}$ to +1 in $\text{Ag}^{+}$, so it loses an electron and is oxidised. Copper goes from +2 to +1, so it gains an electron and is reduced.

$$\text{Cu}^{2+} + \text{Ag} \rightarrow \text{Cu}^{+} + \text{Ag}^{+}$$
Because $\text{Ag}$ is used up here, reaction 3 decreases darkness, it reverses the darkening.

**Spot the catalyst cycle**

Now put 2 and 3 together. Reaction 2 uses up $\text{Cu}^{+}$ and makes $\text{Cu}^{2+}$. Reaction 3 uses up $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ and remakes $\text{Cu}^{+}$. Copper is not consumed overall, it just helps shuttle electrons and is regenerated. That is exactly how a catalyst behaves.

options.A: Correct. Cu+ is consumed in reaction 2 and regenerated in reaction 3, while Cu2+ is formed in reaction 2 and consumed in reaction 3. There is no net loss of copper ions, they provide an alternative route and are reformed, so they act as catalysts.
options.B: False. An oxidising agent is reduced by gaining electrons. In reaction 2, Cu+ loses an electron to form Cu2+, so it is oxidised and acts as a reducing agent. It is the Cl atom that gains an electron to form Cl-, so Cl is the oxidising agent.
options.C: False. Darkness depends on Ag atoms. Reaction 3 converts Ag into Ag+, so it removes the dark species and makes the glass more transparent, not darker. It is the forward direction of reaction 1 that increases darkness.
options.D: False. Reduction is gain of electrons (fall in oxidation number). In reaction 3, Ag (0) becomes Ag+ (+1), so oxidation number increases, electrons are lost. Silver atoms are oxidised, while Cu2+ is reduced to Cu+.
